original.title: A surviving mortal diagonal echo has a distinct death-blocker partner
assumptions: Canonical positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and the named banked lemmas in the source.

exactAuditedStatement: At every canonical row q, each old diagonal echo d(a) with mortal owner a and q<sigma_a maps injectively to the row-q service of sigma_a at a host<a. With L, J, D partitioning old echoes and B0=B-L, Q(q)+2=J+D+2H-B0-F.
hypotheses: q>=0; live means value>q after the row; D includes sigma_a=q, L uses strict q<sigma_a.
Blockers are positive non-diagonal labels; A excludes 0.
proofDependencyMap: Shared canonical foundation: exact positive-MEX/COPY recurrence and P01-P12, independently reconstructed in ../CANONICAL-FOUNDATIONS.md with exact declaration mapping and game interpretation. DEPENDENCIES.json records the additional service lemmas. Final kernel receipts bind the source versions.
FFD: sigma_a<d(a). P11 non-past coverage. Whole-history victim-host exclusion. Row and diagonal injectivity.
independentDerivationAndChecks: For a live mortal echo, q<sigma_a<d(a)<d(q). Thus P11 supplies sigma_a in the prefix and its value>q makes it live. Distinct owners have distinct death labels; otherwise the unique victim at that row would be two columns. Whole-history host exclusion gives host<a, including prebirth services.

Exactly A(q) columns have died by completed row q: each blocker p<=q has one victim, and a victim cannot die twice since COPY persists. Thus m=q+1-A(q). The union of q old diagonals and q prefix labels has d(q)-1+H elements by positive-MEX coverage and maximality; inclusion-exclusion gives d+I+H=2q+1 and Q=2(I+H)-m-1.

The live row partitions into own diagonal, I old diagonals, B blockers, F later-owned diagonals. Diagonal values cannot be frozen; no class overlaps. Hence m=1+I+B+F. Substitute I=L+J+D and B=L+B0 to get Q+2=J+D+2H-B0-F.
At q=0, d=1, A=0, Q=-2 and all residual classes empty, so the constant +2 is correct. Nothing estimates the residual difference or proves Q=o(q).
